name: Bad Bunny
label: Rimas Entertainment
lede: A supermarket bagger from Vega Baja uploads one track to SoundCloud and ends up headlining the Super Bowl in Spanish, with the album Pitchfork ranked No. 5 of 2025 as the reason.

eras.title: The kid in the bunny ears
eras.text: Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio grew up in Almirante Sur, a barrio of Vega Baja, sang in a church choir, and bagged groceries while a scowling childhood photo waited to become a stage name. Puerto Rico's reggaeton and trap lineage, seen from the checkout lane.

years.h: Benito Martínez Ocasio is born in Bayamón, raised in Vega Baja
years.p: His father drove a truck, his mother taught school, and his first musical memory is being handed a Vico C album at age five.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, he grew up in the Almirante Sur barrio with two younger brothers and sang in his church choir until he was 13. He started writing his own songs around 14.

years.big: A scowl in floppy white ears
q: It's not about being a bad person. It's just a name that stuck.
years.h: An Easter costume, a scowl, and a stage name
years.p: At six, Benito wore a bunny costume to a school celebration and hated it. The photo of him glaring under the ears is where "Bad Bunny" comes from.
years.xp:
Yahoo's account has him uploading tracks to SoundCloud under the name while studying audiovisual communications at the University of Puerto Rico at Arecibo and working as a grocery bagger. Wikipedia lists the job as bagger and cashier at an Econo supermarket.

He has said he briefly considered a mask, in the mold of anonymous electronic acts, then decided against hiding.

eras.title: One SoundCloud upload, one phone call
eras.text: A song posted from a supermarket job reaches DJ Luian, and within two years the bagger is on Billboard's Latin chart. Latin trap is the sound, Hear This Music is the door.

years.h: "Diles" goes up on SoundCloud from a Vega Baja checkout job
years.p: DJ Luian hears it and signs the bagger to his label, Hear This Music.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the solo SoundCloud release to January 25, 2016, while Bad Bunny was bagging groceries in Vega Baja. A remix with Ozuna, Farruko, [[Arcángel|47e7833f-f1a7-4703-942d-9acf12f39a1d]] and Ñengo Flow followed on August 26, 2016, produced by Mambo Kingz, DJ Luian and La Paciencia.

The remix's lyric video passed one billion YouTube views by 2023, with no official music video ever made.

years.h: "Soy Peor" is his first solo single
years.p: It reaches No. 19 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs and gets a remix with [[J Balvin|5bdeb32d-56a5-4b6d-a768-264101fa0a0a]], [[Ozuna|f2651b63-a44d-4d1d-ba64-d981d971ecd1]] and Arcángel in 2017.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Bad Bunny and DJ Luian on production and says the song made him the forerunner of Latin trap in the Latin American market. It later went 11x Platinum (Latin) in the U.S.

years.h: "Ahora Me Llama" with Karol G climbs to No. 10 on Hot Latin Songs
years.p: [[Karol G|de22adae-f8ac-414f-b653-b0162611bd60]] gives him his first hit with a partner, and NPR's Alt.Latino calls it one of the year's best Latin songs.

eras.title: Everybody wants a piece
eras.text: A Cardi B hook, a Drake feature and a surprise Christmas Eve album turn a Puerto Rican trap kid into a global name. In 2019 he also picks a side in a political crisis at home.

years.h: "I Like It" with [[Cardi B|2f3c4d70-0462-40da-bba3-0aec5772c556]] and J Balvin tops the Hot 100
years.p: His first No. 1 in the U.S., with Cardi B rapping in English and Bad Bunny and Balvin trading Spanish verses.

years.h: "Mía" with [[Drake|9fff2f8a-21e6-47de-a2b8-7f449929d43f]] reaches No. 5 on the Hot 100
years.p: Drake rides a Bad Bunny single to a top-five hit.

years.h: X 100pre: the debut drops at midnight on Christmas Eve
years.p: Announced the night before via social media, it features [[Diplo|a56bd8f9-8ef8-4d63-89a4-794ed1360dd2]], [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]] and [[Ricky Martin|70ea63ea-70dc-4b63-951a-2c249d2b3b0a]] on backing vocals on "Caro", and peaks at No. 11 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: The title is short for "por siempre." Pitchfork gave it 8.2, Metacritic has it at 84, and Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 41 on its list of the 100 best debut albums.

years.h: Oasis, a full album with J Balvin
years.p: The collaboration reaches No. 9 on the Billboard 200 and tops the U.S. Latin Albums chart.

years.cap: Bad Bunny performing Baile Inolvidable at the 'No me quiero ir de aquí' Residency - Puerto Rico · Wikimedia
yt: "Afilando los Cuchillos" (Residente ft. iLe & Bad Bunny)
years.h: "Afilando los Cuchillos": written and recorded in one day
years.p: With [[Residente|b38a00f2-3746-4e9e-93de-8257ca5b1680]] and iLe, Bad Bunny answers the Telegramgate scandal and joins the protests at the Capitol demanding Governor Ricardo Rosselló resign.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the trio went by "Residents de calle," the track pulled 2.5 million YouTube views in 24 hours, and NPR called it a clear example of a Latin American protest song. Ricky Martin joined them at the Capitol protests.

Bad Bunny's verse hits the government for policing petty crime while underfunding schools.

eras.title: I do what I want
eras.text: With the world in lockdown, he plays a Super Bowl guest slot, drops two albums, performs on a flatbed truck through New York, and becomes the most streamed artist on Spotify. Then he goes to WWE.

years.h: YHLQMDLG: "I do what I want," released on leap day
years.p: It debuts at No. 2, the highest an all-Spanish album had gone, and all 11 tracks chart on the Hot 100 at once.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored it 8.5, calling it a party record that pays tribute to reggaeton's past and future, and the album won the Grammy for Best Latin Pop or Urban Album in 2021. It was also Spotify's most-streamed album of 2020, with 3.3 billion streams.

years.h: "Yo Perreo Sola": the video where he performs in drag
years.p: It tops Billboard's Latin Airplay chart and turns a reggaeton floor-filler into a statement about dancing alone.

years.h: A flatbed truck styled as a subway car rolls through New York
years.p: Bad Bunny plays a surprise concert on top of it, streamed live, and ends at Harlem Hospital Center.

years.src: Wikipedia: El Último Tour Del Mundo
years.h: El Último Tour del Mundo is the first all-Spanish No. 1
years.p: Written during quarantine across Puerto Rico, Mexico and Los Angeles, it swaps party trap for rock, emo and acoustic moods.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.7. It opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 116,000 units, and "Dakiti" with [[Jhay Cortez|2b67658e-429f-425a-adf5-345b13112fc1]] topped the Billboard Global 200. It won Best Música Urbana Album at the 2022 Grammys.

years.h: Royal Rumble: he plays "Booker T" live, then jumps in the ring
years.p: In April he wrestles his first match at WrestleMania 37, teaming with Damian Priest against The Miz and John Morrison.
years.xp: Wikipedia has him attacking The Miz and John Morrison during the Rumble, holding the WWE 24/7 Championship for 28 days, and later feuding with The Judgment Day, ending in a street fight against Priest in San Juan on May 6, 2023.

eras.title: The biggest album on Earth
eras.text: Un Verano Sin Ti spends 13 weeks at No. 1 and turns a summer of reggaeton, bachata and indie pop into a stadium tour. Then he goes quiet, comes back with a rap album, and nobody is sure what's next.

years.h: Un Verano Sin Ti is Spotify's most-streamed album ever
years.p: It spends 13 weeks at No. 1 and becomes the first Spanish-language album nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored it 8.4 and named it Best New Music. Wikipedia reports it topped the 2022 Billboard 200 year-end chart, a first for a Spanish-language album. The cover, by Adrian Hernandez (Ugly Primo), shows a sad one-eyed heart against a beach.

years.h: World's Hottest Tour becomes the top-grossing tour by a Latin artist
years.p: It plays 14 American countries and, per Wikipedia, grosses $232.5 million.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana
years.h: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana is a 22-track rap record
years.p: It debuts at No. 1 with 184,000 units and all 21 eligible tracks chart on the Hot 100.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Isabella Herrera scored it 7.4, calling it a rap homecoming that is bloated but thematically focused. Guests include [[Eladio Carrión|239e3283-3b23-4606-8c3b-b5c3bd80313d]], [[Feid|eaee97f6-f2e4-414a-966c-f31a1fb4696a]] and [[Young Miko|c4442130-e7f2-40aa-bcab-b921cc45a365]]. He told Vanity Fair he was pushing toward a new mood shaped by 1970s music.
play: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana

eras.title: Two chairs and a coliseum
eras.text: He goes back to plena, salsa and bomba, records a love letter to Puerto Rico, and refuses to play it in the mainland U.S. Instead he plays it for the island, night after night.

years.src: Wikipedia: Debí Tirar Más Fotos · Rolling Stone: Bad Bunny Makes · Pitchfork Review substack
years.h: DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS: the record that recommits him to Puerto Rico
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.8 and ranked it No. 5 of 2025. Two plastic chairs on a patch of dirt fronting a banana grove sit on the cover.
years.xp:
Released January 5, 2025 on Rimas Entertainment, the 17-track album leans on plena, jíbaro, salsa and bomba over production from [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]], MAG and La Paciencia, with Los Pleneros de la Cresta, RaiNao, Chuwi, Omar Courtz and Dei V. Metacritic has it at 95, and Rolling Stone's Maya Georgi gave it five stars, hailing "a whole new peak of greatness."

"Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii" tackles gentrification, and "La Mudanza" closes with a promise not to leave. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 before climbing to No. 1 the following week.

years.h: "DtMF" gets a video and becomes the album's face
years.p: A plena and Nintendo-style-beat lament for photos not taken becomes a TikTok tribute to lost relatives.
years.xp: It debuted at No. 38 on the Hot 100, then hit No. 1 after the Super Bowl, his first solo No. 1 in the U.S., per Wikipedia. It was nominated for Record and Song of the Year at the 2026 Grammys.

years.h: NPR Tiny Desk with a full Puerto Rican band
years.p: Bad Bunny takes the plena and jíbaro sounds of the new record to the NPR office.

years.h: The world tour announcement skips the U.S. mainland
years.p: Wikipedia reports the 23 stadium dates avoid the continental U.S. over concerns about immigration enforcement at shows.

years.cap: José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum, San Juan
years.src: Wikipedia: No Me Quiero Ir de Aquí
years.h: No Me Quiero Ir de Aquí: about 30 nights at El Choliseo
years.p: The first nine shows are reserved for people living in Puerto Rico. Sundays, guests take over "Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii."
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts 31 sold-out shows and more than 500,000 fans, the first residency the coliseum or Puerto Rico had hosted. Guests included Residente, Rauw Alejandro, Ivy Queen, Ozuna and Nicky Jam, with [[Rubén Blades|f050673a-dfb3-4200-b057-bf78213de36c]] and [[Luis Fonsi|d68fda90-ab8d-4799-be56-317ba4ae700f]] taking Sunday turns.

Studies put the economic impact between $176.6 million and $733 million, and hotel occupancy rose 6 percent in July.

years.h: Announced as the Super Bowl LX halftime headliner
years.p: He becomes the first solo Latino artist to headline. Donald Trump called the pick "absolutely ridiculous," per Wikipedia.

eras.title: The whole country watches
eras.text: The album that skipped the mainland gets the biggest stage in American entertainment, and the biggest prize at the Grammys.

years.big: Before I say thanks to God: ICE out.
q: Before I say thanks to God, I'm going to say: ICE out
years.src: Wikipedia: Bad Bunny · Wikipedia: Debí Tirar Más Fotos
yt: Bad Bunny wins Album of the Year, 2026 Grammys
years.h: Grammys: first all-Spanish Album of the Year
years.p: Accepting Best Música Urbana Album earlier in the night, Bad Bunny opened with that line to a standing ovation. DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS later won Album of the Year, and he dedicated it to immigrants who left home to follow their dreams.
years.xp: He was the first Latino artist nominated in all three of the Grammys' big categories in the same year, with "DtMF" up for Record and Song of the Year. Per Wikipedia, artists including Billie Eilish and Jack Antonoff wore "ICE Out" pins.

years.src: Wikipedia: Super Bowl LX halftime show
yt: Bad Bunny's Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show
years.h: Super Bowl LX: a sugarcane field and a wedding, mostly in Spanish
years.p: Lady Gaga plays a salsa "Die with a Smile"; Ricky Martin sings "Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii."
years.xp:
More than 300 dancers worked the field, a casita section drew Cardi B, Karol G and Pedro Pascal, and a real couple was married on stage with Bad Bunny signing as witness. Wikipedia counts 128.2 million U.S. viewers, the fourth-most-watched halftime show.

Trump called it "absolutely terrible," and conservative groups programmed a rival All-American Halftime Show with Kid Rock, though the FCC found no violations.
